title: Word 13 — On Eternity
attribution_note: Word 13 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: Nothing moves a sinner to repentance as eternity does, and nothing is as profitable for every Christian as the remembrance and contemplation of eternity. Eternity restrains a man from sin, tames the passions, turns him away from the world and all its vanity, breaks the heart, gives birth to tears of repentance, stirs him to prayer, and produces true sighing of the heart. The remembrance and contemplation of eternity can correct even the most depraved. Contemplation of eternity filled the deserts, caves, mountains, and earthly chasms with dwellers. Contemplating eternity, the holy martyrs chose to endure the harshest torments rather than submit to the will of impious kings and deny Christ. From contemplation of eternity, robbers, murderers, plunderers, fornicators and harlots, and other grievous sinners became saints and God's chosen ones.

sections.heading: The forgetfulness of the present age

pairs.en: Beloved Christians! Let us imprint eternity upon our memory, and then we will abide unchangingly in constant, true repentance, contrition of heart, and prayer, and will be enticed by no vanity of this world, and will turn away from every sin as from a venomous serpent. Everything that pleases the sons of this age and seems to them agreeable and precious will become loathsome to us. Indeed, we will be content with a crust of bread, a small hut, and the coarsest clothing. The remembrance and contemplation of eternity will teach us to be content with these.

Eternity is twofold: most blessed and most wretched. In the most blessed eternity there will be the kingdom of God; there will be God, whom man shall see face to face; there will be joy and ineffable gladness; soul and body will receive their all-perfect blessedness, and man will be granted those good things which *“eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have entered into the heart of man”* [1 Corinthians 2:9]. *“Then the righteous will shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father”* [Matthew 13:43]. In the wretched eternity there will be deprivation and separation from God, and every suffering and torment in body and soul. Then people will wish to die, but death will flee from them. This is the second death, the eternal death.

Sinners! We hear the Word of God about eternity, and we see that eternity is twofold: blessed, filled with joy and every good thing, that is, eternal life; and wretched, filled with torments, sorrow, sicknesses, and every evil, that is, eternal death. Let us therefore repent and wash our sins with tears, that we may escape the wretched eternity and enter into eternal life and the kingdom of God. After Christ's Dread Judgment, each will go to his own eternity, for then Christ the Judge will render to all their due sentence. To the righteous He will open the doors of His eternal kingdom and say to them: *“Come, you blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world”* [Matthew 25:34]. But to sinners He will say: *“Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels”* [Matthew 25:41]. *“And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life”* [Matthew 25:46]. Remember us also, O Lord, in Your kingdom! Amen.
